text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I ran a short nsys trace on cluster-3 during the canary. Full tracing shows a ~12-18% p50 CPU/GPU latency bump when we enable kernel timeline capture. We need a low-overhead plan for prod profiling (sampling + safe fallback).

sam: Agreed. Full nsys in prod is too noisy. Two ideas: (1) sparse/periodic sampling windows, (2) event-based sampling on KV cache misses only.

oliver: +1. For KV cache, only sample when cache_miss_count % 100 == 0 (or use probabilistic sampling). Hits are common and adding probes there skews numbers.

anya: Also flagging that batching heuristics change distribution; we should correlate batch sizes with kernel-choice changes in traces. If sample windows are too short we miss those shifts.

sam: Example lightweight sampler I used (pseudo):
```bash
# run every 5m, capture 10s of trace at 2Hz sampling
while true; do 
  if [[ $(date +%s) -lt $END ]]; then break; fi
  nsys profile --output /tmp/prof-$(date +%s) 
    --trace=cuda --sample=cpu --sample-freq=200 
    --duration=10s &
  sleep 300
done
```
Note: reduced --sample-freq and short duration to keep overhead < ~5%.

maya: Can you attach the exact nsys flags you used in the canary run? Was kernel timeline enabled?

sam: Canary flags (actual):
```
nsys profile --output /mnt/traces/run-1923456789 
  --sample=cpu --sample-freq=400 
  --trace=cuda,kernels,osrt 
  --capture-range=nvtx --stop-on-exec=false 
  --duration=20s
```
Timeline+kernels = heavy. Shortening to 8-10s and freq=200 cut CPU overhead roughly in half in my tests.

oliver: Measured numbers from cluster-3:
- full timeline (20s, freq400): p50 increase ~15% , tail (p95) shift ~8%
- short sample (10s, freq200): p50 increase ~4% , tail ~2%
- event-only sampling (miss-only, 10s): p50 increase ~1.2%
So event-only looks promising.

anya: Important: sampling affects batching behaviour. Observed that when tracing is on, the runtime's dynamic batcher reduces max batch size by ~10% (it senses latency). That changes kernel selection and can hide the actual hotspot. We need a fallback that marks sampled traces as 'probe' so runtime ignores them for batching decisions.

maya: Proposal for safe-prod profiling guardrails: list below — feedback welcome.
1) Probe mode must be opt-in with env var REDWOOD_PROFILER=probe and token-based allowlist.
2) Rate limit: token bucket 2 traces per node per 5 minutes.
3) Prefer event-triggered sampling: sample_on = ["kv_miss", "cold_start", "model_load"] with configurable prob.
4) Probe traces flagged in telemetry so production autoscaling/batching logic excludes them.
5) Auto-fallback: if p50 measured overhead > 7% or error rate increases, kill profiler for 30m and alert on #eng-runtime.
6) Minimal trace mode (no kernel timeline) for continuous low-overhead sampling; full timeline allowed only for short triage windows.

sam: Implementation notes: token-bucket is easiest to enforce at agent level (profiler-agent on node). We can store bucket state in local mem and reconcile to control plane occasionally.

oliver: For event-triggered sampling, easiest hook is in kv_get path:
- if miss -> sample with probability p_miss (default 0.01)
- attach nvtx markers around the request to capture the exact sequence
This keeps sampling focused on behaviors we care about.

anya: Also add an internal metric: profiler_probe_in_flight and profiler_cpu_overhead_estimate (running EMA). That lets us implement the auto-fallback rule.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of profiler-agent v0.8 started on pool=cluster-3. Trace capture disabled by default.

maya: For triage sessions where we need full kernels: schedule a short maintenance window, flip REDWOOD_PROFILER=full for targeted hosts only, and run with explicit start/stop controls (don't leave it on).

sam: Quick practical tip: don't enable synchronous logging in the profiler path. That alone can add a few ms per request. Use buffered NVTX and async uploader for trace files.

oliver: We should add a lightweight end-to-end test that validates the profiling guardrail behaviour: enable probe, simulate high QPS, assert profiler in/out obeys token bucket and auto-disable triggers.

maya: I'll write the runbook and add it to eng-runtime/playbooks. Plan: implement token-bucket + event-only sampling + telemetry flags this sprint. If nobody objects, I'll open a PR with the config schema and runtime checks.

anya: No objections. One more ask: include a mode for "sample only misses with full timeline for 5s" so we can capture exact kernels for representative misses.

sam: +1, but make that mode gated behind a human approval step in console (to avoid accidental widespread full traces).

maya: Sounds good. I'll start PR today and ping for review. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: profiler-bot: probe metric profiler_cpu_overhead_estimate=1.7% noted for node=node-17 (from the short sample).
